# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 2 (Bi-Vb Pc2)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc2  
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 2  
**Title (English, from literature):** Removing pubic hair  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 2, titled *Sambādhaloma* (“Removing pubic hair”), is an expiation rule governing Buddhist nuns (*bhikkhunī*s) in the Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule establishes that a nun who removes hair from her groin or armpits commits an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [Horner]. In the canonical analysis, the term *sambādha* is specifically defined as the armpits and the private parts [Horner]. As examined by Ute Hüsken, the introductory account (*vatthu*, Vin IV 260) targets the practice of removing or shaving pubic hair (*sambādhe lomaṃ saṃharāpeti*)—likened to the behavior of laywomen—rather than naked bathing, which is regulated separately under Pācittiya 21 [Hüsken 1997].

 Modern English translations of the rule include those by I.B. Horner and Bhikkhu Brahmali [Horner].
